paper_metadata.title: Quantum Amplitude Loading for Rainbow Options Pricing

summary: The paper presents an end-to-end gate-based quantum algorithm for rainbow option pricing using Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) on the IBM QASM noiseless simulator. The proof-of-concept uses 24 qubits, 1000 shots, two assets, a strike price of $190, and reports a classically computed expected payoff of $23.0238 for validation; two exponential amplitude-loading variants are analyzed, but only T-depth formulas are given rather than a full circuit depth.

experiments.description: End-to-end gate-based quantum pricing of two-asset rainbow options using Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) with two alternative exponential amplitude-loading implementations (integration and direct) on the IBM QASM noiseless simulator.

algorithm.variant: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) for rainbow option pricing with delayed transition to price space
algorithm.convergence_criteria: IQAE run with precision ϵ = 0.01 and confidence interval parameter α = 0.05

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Gaussian log-return distributions are loaded into qubit registers; correlated multivariate normal samples are generated via Cholesky decomposition; the maximum asset value is computed in return space; payoff is encoded into the amplitude of a target qubit using a comparator plus either direct or integration-based exponential amplitude loading.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the expected discounted payoff of a rainbow call option, with payoff max(M_t - K, 0) where M_t is the maximum asset price at maturity and K is the strike price.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Comparator-based branching on whether z >= (log(K)-b')/b; delayed strike subtraction handled classically in post-processing; no penalty terms.

problem_instance.description: Two-asset rainbow option pricing example using real-world market data; assets start at S0_1 = $193.97 and S0_2 = $189.12; strike K = $190; maturity 250 days.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Historical daily log-returns are used to estimate mean and covariance; Cholesky decomposition is applied to the correlation matrix; Gaussian distributions are discretized with two qubits per asset; arithmetic is rounded to one decimal place.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 1000 shots per experiment; measured the objective qubit after the IQAE subroutine; compared simulator estimates against a classically computed expected payoff of $23.0238.

hardware.classical_solver: classical Monte Carlo / classical expected-value computation for validation

implementation_details.classical_solver: classical computation of expected payoff for validation
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Historical log-returns used to estimate mean and covariance; Gaussian discretization; Cholesky decomposition; scaling relative to first asset; arithmetic rounding to one decimal place.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Post-processing of IQAE estimate to reconstruct expected payoff and apply discounting; delayed strike subtraction handled classically.

classical_baselines.name: classical expected payoff computation
classical_baselines.description: Classical estimation of the expected payoff accounting for discretization and arithmetic precision for comparison with quantum simulator results.

speedup_claims.conditions: Amplitude Estimation used for expectation estimation; quantum sample complexity scales as O(1/M) versus classical Monte Carlo O(1/sqrt(M))
speedup_claims.caveats: Claim is asymptotic/theoretical; no wall-clock speedup or hardware benchmark shown.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Quadratic improvement in sample complexity via amplitude estimation; expectation estimation scales as O(1/M) in samples versus classical Monte Carlo O(1/sqrt(M))
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(1/sqrt(M)) Monte Carlo convergence for sample-based estimation

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 24 logical qubits in noiseless IBM QASM simulation; 1000 shots; IQAE with precision 0.01 and alpha 0.05; no hardware benchmark or wall-clock comparison reported.
limiting_factors: Only asymptotic quadratic sample-complexity improvement is discussed
No crossover analysis or constant-factor benchmark
State preparation and arithmetic dominate circuit complexity
Classical baseline only used for validation

notes: Circuit depth was not explicitly reported as a single total depth; only T-depth formulas and a 24-qubit simulation size were given, so circuit_depth remains null and no transpiled depth was reported.
Hardware type inferred as simulator_other because the paper explicitly states IBM QASM noiseless simulator rather than a real QPU.
The paper reports a noiseless simulator validation and a classical expected-payoff comparison, but no demonstrated quantum advantage.
